instruction.text: This is a map of Alaska and Western Canada. Select the bird to learn more.

hint.label: Boreal forest
hint.text: The boreal forest is the largest land biome on Earth. This evergreen forest wraps around the northern parts of the globe, stretching across North America, Europe and Asia.

atoms.b: The Canadian boreal forest is known as the Bird Nursery of North America, as billions of ((++birds insects)) migrate there during the spring and summer months.
This forest covers 1.9 billion hectares, which is almost 60% of the country’s ((++land water)) area.
Many indigenous communities still live there today and continue to ((++practise avoid)) long-standing traditions and uses of the land.

trainers.instruction: Read the text and select the matching image.

text.text: The Canadian Shield covers almost 50% of Canada’s total landmass!

atoms.a: The Canadian Shield is one of the oldest geological areas on Earth. It has many ancient rocks, some of which are over four billion years old!
The Canadian Shield is rich in natural minerals, such as gold and diamonds.
The Canadian Shield has many lakes and swamps because of glacial erosion during the last Ice Age.
The bodies of water are ideal for producing large amounts of hydroelectricity.

hint.label: Seven Summits
hint.text:
The Seven Summits are the tallest mountains on each continent:

1. Mount Everest (Asia) - 8,849 m
2. Aconcagua (South America) - 6,961 m
3. Denali (North America) - 6,194 m
4. Mount Kilimanjaro (Africa) - 5,895 m
5. Mount Elbrus (Europe) - 5,642 m
6. Mount Vinson (Antarctica) - 4,892 m
7. Mount Kosciuszko (Australia) - 2,228 m
hint.sound: The Seven Summits are the tallest mountains on each continent.

atoms.b: Denali is North America’s tallest ((++mountain lake)) and is located in Alaska. It is the third highest of the Seven Summits.
The name Denali comes from a ((++language symbol)) of the Alaskan Native peoples. It translates to “the high one”.
The mountain is incredibly ((++difficult easy)) to climb due to extreme weather and its steep terrain. The success rate of this summit is just over 50%.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Toronto is the most populated city in Canada with around 3.2 million people. In contrast, Iqaluit is only home to around 7,500 residents, despite it being the capital of the territory of Nunavut.
atoms.sound: Toronto is the most populated city in Canada with around 3.2 million people. In contrast, Iqaluette is only home to around 7,500 residents, despite it being the capital of the territory of Nunavut.

atoms.text: This is the largest but least densely populated territory in Canada. Nunavut’s harsh polar climate makes it difficult for people to live there, so the region is home to only 0.1% of Canada’s total population.
Most large cities in Canada are located in an area called the Québec City-Windsor Corridor. Here, the weather is warmer and the land is flatter. Around 50% of all Canadians live in this region.

What is the name of the area in Canada that Toronto is located in?
